entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — 2026-09-24

Today's batch is headlined by the Hermes Desktop live screen streaming launch, the Hermes Agent v0.21.4 release with machine-readable output, and a pair of deep dives on how the Hermes-Claude plugin keeps your credentials safe. Plenty to dig into.

Releases

Hermes Desktop now streams your agent's screen live. @NousResearch and @Teknium announced that Hermes Desktop can live-stream any agent's screen in real time, paired with interactive desktop passthrough so you can visually access the same machine your agent controls. It was the batch's biggest story by a wide margin (~397k views, ~2k likes), with celebratory sentiment framing it as a long-awaited feature finally shipped — @Teknium's "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" captured the mood.

Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (released 21 Sep 2026) adds a --format stream-json CLI flag that emits machine-readable JSONL output — a practical upgrade if you're scripting or piping agent output programmatically.

AgentProto v0.20.0 (released 22 Sep 2026) is a new Apache-2.0 TypeScript agent runtime that launched with integrations for 14 agents including Hermes — a standardized new integration path, and a sign of broader multi-agent interoperability efforts.

Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 centers on MCP security hardening via scoped sessions. Paired with Hermes v0.21.4's configurable MCP discovery concurrency, it signals MCP maturing into security-sensitive, load-bearing infrastructure that agent frameworks must now harden and tune — relevant background for any MCP-dependent Hermes setup.

Merged PRs

Hermes Agent v0.21.4 rolled up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, carrying the new --format stream-json flag alongside skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.

Community

  • @rlaope delivered the batch's most substantive community-led extension of the Hermes tooling ecosystem: an [oh-my-hermes (OMH)](/?date=2026-09-24&category=social#item-415aecf318f8) update adding Jev-Skills and model routing to hermes-agent workflows, plus a dual open-source drop headlined by jeval for evaluating and visually extracting Jev results.
  • @Teknium was hands-on all day: pushing back on a reported cache issue and demanding reproducible steps, shipping a quick fix in response to user feedback ("fixed lol"), and clarifying that a tool under discussion is built by NousResearch, not Anthropic.
  • Light side commentary: @rlaope called the freshly released Claude Opus 5.5 "crazy" — in the impressive sense — while staying lukewarm on Claude Code.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Watch your agents work. An official walkthrough video and documentation from @tonbistudio cover the new Hermes Desktop live streaming and desktop passthrough (542 likes on the walkthrough).
  • Run Hermes via iMessage. Official guidance walks through running Hermes via iMessage with any model (121 likes, ~13k views).
  • How the Hermes-Claude plugin actually works. Two deep dives unpack the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: the pipeline drives the unmodified official claude CLI with process isolation, tool-inventory mapping, and a one-request admission relay over stream-json transport. Authentication keeps credentials entirely inside the official CLI via claude auth login — the no-API-key-exposed design is the central security property. Well worth a read before wiring your own subscription into Hermes.

entry.title: Research Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: This section leads with the Hermes Agent v0.21.4 release (21 September 2026), which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag for machine-readable JSONL output, rolled up with skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency across ~1,812 merged PRs — a practical upgrade for anyone scripting or piping agent output. Two deep-dives then unpack the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: its pipeline drives the unmodified official claude CLI with process isolation, tool-inventory mapping, and a one-request admission relay over stream-json transport, while authentication keeps credentials entirely inside the official CLI via claude auth login, so no API keys are exposed to Hermes. Rounding out the ecosystem: AgentProto v0.20.0, a new open-source (Apache-2.0) TypeScript agent runtime that explicitly lists Hermes among its 14 integrated agents — an easy new integration path for Hermes users — and Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, whose MCP security hardening (scoped sessions) offers relevant background for MCP-dependent Hermes setups.

entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: Bot Screen / Live Desktop launch (dominant story): @NousResearch's announcement that Hermes Desktop now live-streams any agent's screen in real time (1967 likes, ~397k views — the batch's biggest reach) and @Teknium's launch of interactive desktop passthrough (1145 likes, 173k views) anchor the section, supported by an official @tonbistudio walkthrough video with docs (542 likes) and @Teknium amplifying the guide. Community sentiment is celebratory and reads as long-awaited demand finally shipped — @Teknium's 'Finallllly!' and 'Much needed!' (200 likes, 20k views) signal pent-up enthusiasm. OMH / Jev ecosystem: @rlaope delivered the batch's most substantive community update — the oh-my-hermes (OMH) release adding Jev-Skills and model routing to hermes-agent workflows — plus a dual OSS drop headlined by jeval (Jev evaluation/visualization); a redundant shorter jeval post and bare link shares were deprioritized. Maintainer support & shipping: @Teknium's hands-on presence stands out — pushing back on a reported cache issue and demanding reproducible steps, shipping a quick fix in response to user feedback ('fixed lol'), and clarifying a discussed tool is built by NousResearch, not Anthropic. Usage tips: official guidance to run Hermes via iMessage with any model (121 likes, 13k views). Side commentary: @rlaope called Claude Opus 5.5 'crazy' (impressive) while staying lukewarm on Claude Code — light sentiment around the freshly released Anthropic model.
